central_topic: Conditional gains and limitations of cross-fitted nonlinear frozen-score control variates for population-mean confidence intervals with fixed labeled data, unlabeled data, and predictor.
core_methods: Prediction-powered population-mean estimation with independent labeled and unlabeled samples
Training-only affine and spline/ridge score calibration with finite-unlabeled-sample control weighting
Nested risk-based selection among zero, affine, and nonlinear controls
Within-fold offset-invariant studentization with shared-unlabeled-pool covariance
Regularized signed covariance stacking of affine and nonlinear score controls
comparators: Label-only Student-t and Clopper-Pearson mean/proportion intervals
Classical control variates with estimated coefficients
Cross-Prediction-Powered Inference and double/debiased machine learning as conceptual cross-fitting comparators, not executed baselines
benchmarks: ppi-python gene_expression frozen outcome/prediction table, sourced in the local manifest to Vaishnav et al., Nature 603, 455-463 (2022); independent resampling targets the local empirical-source mean
Synthetic Bernoulli mean cases: linear, nonlinear, uninformative, and rare_outcome with frozen scalar predictor f(X)=X
architectural_shifts: Score post-processing only: affine calibration versus small spline/ridge calibration, discrete family selection versus signed two-control covariance stacking; no predictor-backbone change or supported architecture-transfer claim
result_driven_themes: Dataset-specific narrowing: final gene_expression mean per-seed width ratio to the implemented PPI++ baseline is approximately 0.9423; other cases do not establish uniform improvement
Observed coverage is repeated-sampling evidence, not a finite-sample guarantee for learned controls or the adaptive fallback procedure
Rare-outcome behavior motivates exact-binomial versus Wald coverage/width tradeoffs; zero-width baseline intervals make aggregate per-seed width ratios fragile
Constant and permuted score controls motivate limits of usable prediction information; affine/nonlinear oracle headroom is an analytical motivation, not a demonstrated universal efficiency bound
Smooth covariance stacking did not establish dominance over risk-based family selection; no paired learner ablation or causal attribution is available
